answers: Significant progress has been made, but challenges remain. Data management and curation are now priorities, leading to engineering of high-quality, flexible databases and APIs for materials data mining. High-throughput computations and text-mining approaches have emerged as new paradigms, shifting focus to extracting knowledge from voluminous materials datasets. However, the field faces critical hurdles including data veracity and integrity, integrating diverse experimental and computational data, ensuring data longevity, standardization, and bridging the gap between industrial and academic efforts.

Significant progress in data mining within materials science has been made, shifting focus toward data management, curation, and analysis. High-throughput computations and big data have transformed the field, enabling the engineering of high-quality databases with flexible graphical interfaces and APIs. Text mining and natural language processing (NLP) approaches have also been applied, with substantial efforts made in retrieving useful information from materials science publications, though the field is still at the early developmental stage of these methods. Despite the progress, researchers identify five critical challenges that impede full realization of data-driven materials science potential.
